The Staff Data Engineer will support the development of advanced data engineering and applied data science solutions for clients across the utility and energy sectors. This hands-on role combines data pipeline development, data architecture, statistical modeling, and machine learning to turn complex utility data into actionable intelligence. You will work with diverse datasets, including smart meter readings, grid operations, geographic information systems, and customer information. Collaborating with client teams and senior technical experts, you will design reliable data workflows and contribute to scalable analytical solutions. Your work will help utilities improve forecasting, operational insights, and data-driven decision-making. This is an opportunity to contribute to modernizing energy infrastructure and building a more resilient, efficient, and sustainable power grid.

Accountabilities

You will deliver technical workstreams across data engineering, architecture, and applied data science, translating client requirements into reliable data solutions and analytical models while ensuring quality, scalability, and clear technical communication.

Explore and assess utility datasets, including advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) interval data, SCADA, GIS, asset information, customer programs, and billing records.
Design, develop, test, and maintain repeatable ETL/ELT pipelines that ingest, transform, reconcile, and deliver data from databases, files, APIs, and other approved sources.
Build reusable Python and SQL components for data cleansing, standardization, aggregation, validation, and feature preparation.
Profile source data and implement automated quality checks covering completeness, validity, consistency, uniqueness, and freshness.
Develop record-matching and entity-resolution logic to reconcile customer, asset, device, program, and operational records.
Troubleshoot pipeline failures, data inconsistencies, and performance issues, documenting findings and corrective actions.

Evaluate and document architectural trade-offs involving relational databases, warehouses, lakehouses, batch processing, APIs, scalability, performance, maintainability, and cost.

Develop and validate forecasting models, classification approaches, anomaly detection, clustering methods, and prioritization models using utility datasets.
Address modeling challenges such as overfitting, class imbalance, sampling bias, and time-dependent validation.
Monitor model performance and support documented recalibration, retraining, and ongoing model updates.

Clearly communicate model assumptions, uncertainty, limitations, and the distinction between observed, inferred, and predicted results.
Participate in requirements workshops, technical interviews, architecture reviews, and client working sessions.
Prepare technical reports, process maps, architecture documentation, and analytical presentations.
Deliver assigned work within agreed scope, schedules, budgets, and quality expectations.

The ideal candidate combines practical data engineering expertise with applied statistical and machine learning experience, a solid understanding of utility-sector data, and the ability to communicate technical solutions effectively to diverse stakeholders.

jobs.title: Head of Data Science, Intelligence Ventures
jobs.description:
This role requires the ability to work lawfully in the U.S. without employment-based immigration sponsorship, now or in the future.

The Head of Data Science builds the models that turn a new AI-native behavioral intelligence platform into products customers buy, and proves to those customers that the products work. At the core of the platform, part of Spectrum Intelligence Ventures, is a proprietary transformer-based model that learns how households behave from network-scale signal and encodes that behavior as embeddings. Those embeddings are the foundation for audiences, insights, measurement, and data licenses sold to brands, agencies, and ad tech, media, and AI platforms. Over the next 18 to 24 months, this leader’s job is to get that portfolio to market and make it stand up to buyer scrutiny: build the predictive models and products on top of the embedding layer, set the evidence standard buyers will test them against, and work alongside product and sales to scope pilots, answer technical buyers, and convert evaluations into contracts. In parallel, this leader owns the direction of the embedding model itself, working with the Head of Technology and external development partners, and is accountable for showing that it delivers performance conventional approaches cannot. The Head of Data Science builds and leads the data science team, sits on the platform leadership team, and reports directly to the Head of Intelligence Ventures.

How The Head Of Data Science Makes An Impact

Build and run the predictive models behind the platform’s audience and data products, including in-market, life-stage, purchase propensity, category interest, lifestyle affinity, and behavioral velocity models scored daily at the household level across more than two dozen verticals. Own segment definitions, coverage, refresh cadence, and measured accuracy for every audience the platform sells, whether through Spectrum Reach, DSP data marketplaces, or partner platforms.
Own the platform’s Feature Store as a commercial product: named, typed, versioned, and documented features that serve audiences, insights, measurement, and partner models. Lead the outcome anchoring program that trains and calibrates models against licensed third-party outcome data (vehicle registrations, mortgage originations, card and SKU-level retail spend, travel bookings, and similar sources) so that propensity scores mean what they say, and automate feature creation as new signal sources come online.
Lead the modeling behind custom and partner-specific audiences, including seed-based lookalike expansion, profile-based audience construction, and site- or CRM-seeded models that identify households entering a brand’s purchase path before they reach the brand. Establish repeatable, clean-room-based workflows with transparent match rates, expansion multiples, and performance against the buyer’s own baseline.
Design and defend the platform’s measurement methodology, including exposed-versus-control campaign lift using matched behavioral controls, test-and-holdout incrementality, and closed-loop validation against real-world outcomes. Define the journey, demand, and category metrics that power insights subscriptions and aggregate demand indices, built to withstand scrutiny from brand marketing science teams, agency analytics groups, and measurement partners.
Lead the data science behind the platform’s identity and viewing products: the adjudication and confidence calibration methods that verify partner household graphs against network ground truth, and the household viewing-state, trajectory, and reachability models that underpin viewing intelligence for programmers, agencies, and measurement companies.
Direct the roadmap for the platform’s proprietary transformer-based behavioral embedding model, a multi-entity architecture that encodes both a stable household profile and short-term intent, working with the Head of Technology and external development partners on architecture, training, and refresh. Hold the embedding layer to a commercial standard: measured lift over attribute-only and engineered-feature baselines in the audiences, lookalikes, measurement, and partner models it feeds.
Establish the evaluation, MLOps, and responsible AI standards for every model the platform ships, including evaluation cards that state accuracy, calibration, and coverage in a form buyers can cite; automated release gates; monitoring and drift detection; bias and fairness testing; and privacy-preserving techniques such as audience floors, differential privacy, and adversarial testing, in partnership with Legal and Privacy.
Serve as the senior data science voice with customers and partners, including brand analytics and insights leaders, agency data science teams, and DSPs, identity providers, measurement companies, and AI platforms. Scope pilots and evaluations with product, sales, and solutions teams, and translate methodology into clear commercial proof points.
Build and lead a team of data scientists, ML engineers, and measurement scientists matched to the work ahead: strong in applied predictive modeling and measurement, with the deep learning depth to take greater ownership of the embedding layer over time. Set hiring priorities, operating cadence, and a culture of rigorous experimentation with a clear bias toward production deployment and revenue impact.

Required Qualifications

Proven record leading data science for data, audience, identity, targeting, or measurement products in the advertising, media, or marketing ecosystem, where models are packaged, priced, sold, and renewed by external buyers
Deep, hands-on expertise in predictive modeling on consumer-level data at scale, including propensity and response modeling, classification, gradient boosting, regression, calibration, segmentation and clustering, and lookalike modeling, with sound judgment about which method fits the commercial problem
Strong grounding in measurement and causal inference, including incrementality testing, matched and synthetic controls, test-and-holdout design, and the practical limits of attribution and media mix approaches
Working knowledge of identity and data collaboration: household and device graphs, onboarding and match rates, clean rooms (Snowflake, LiveRamp, AWS, or equivalent), identity namespaces such as RampID and UID2, and the use of licensed third-party data in modeling
Command of the full data science lifecycle in production, from feature engineering through training, validation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration, at large dataset scale (billions, even trillions of records); experience designing feature stores and scoring pipelines that serve audiences and partner deliveries
Hands-on proficiency with Python, SQL, and distributed data processing (Spark or equivalent); experience running ML workloads on Snowflake, Databricks, AWS, or equivalent cloud platforms
Solid working knowledge of deep learning and representation learning, including embeddings, sequence models, and transformers, sufficient to direct an embedding roadmap with external partners, set its evaluation standards, and put embeddings to work as features in downstream models
Familiarity with privacy-preserving analytics and consumer data regulation, including aggregation thresholds, differential privacy, and consent management; comfortable working alongside Legal and Privacy on product design
Ability to explain methodology clearly to executives, sellers, and buyers, and to defend it under scrutiny from sophisticated technical counterparts in external partner and customer conversations
Track record of building and growing high-performing data science teams, ideally from an early stage, and recruiting senior talent in competitive markets
Curiosity about the application of AI to consumer intelligence, including how foundation models and AI agents can draw on behavioral context to make better decisions

Required Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, or a related quantitative field

Preferred Education

Master’s degree or PhD in Statistics, Machine Learning, Econometrics, Operations Research, or a related quantitative discipline; an advanced degree is valued but not required, and a record of applied commercial impact is weighted equally

Required Related Work Experience And Number Of Years

Experience leading applied data science or analytics teams that build data, audience, identity, or measurement products: 7 years
Hands-on predictive modeling, machine learning, or measurement science on consumer-level data at scale: 10 years

Preferred Related Work Experience And Number Of Years

Applied deep learning or representation learning (embeddings, sequence models) deployed in production on consumer behavioral data: 3 years

Olivo Sciences is a precision medicine company focused on helping patients with brain disorders live longer, healthier lives by bringing AI-driven precision to therapeutic development and personalized care.

Olivo is solving this problem by building a large-scale multimodal data library focused on neurology, neuro-oncology, psychiatry, and neurosurgery. Its platform brings together clinical, imaging, molecular, and other healthcare data and uses AI to help improve drug discovery, clinical trial design, patient enrollment, and real-world evidence generation.

Olivo has already established relationships with leading healthcare and research organizations and is building a growing network of hospital, clinic, laboratory, and research partners.

Olivo Sciences is seeking accomplished life sciences executives to join its Strategic Advisory Board and help guide the company’s work across neuroscience and clinical trials.

Lead and develop a team of data scientists – hire, empower, and coach team members; set a high bar for analytical quality and career growth.

What Are We Doing?

Our foundational science enables the generation and directed differentiation of universal pluripotent stem cells into authentic, functional cells for allogeneic cellular therapies.

BlueRock Therapeutics, a wholly-owned and independently operated subsidiary of Bayer AG, is a leading engineered cell therapy company using its unique cell+gene

The Laboratory Technician plays a key role in supporting snack processing operations by conducting chemical and physical analyses and providing technical support to leadership. Perform a full range of laboratory analyses related to snack processing, demonstrating strong technical competency and accuracy.
Maintain familiarity with all laboratory equipment, chemicals, and reagents, and use them safely and effectively.
Collect, prepare, label, and organize raw material and product samples for analysis in accordance with established procedures.

Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support laboratory, quality, and production objectives.

Essential Skills

Demonstrated knowledge and familiarity with laboratory operations and quality control functions in a food or related manufacturing environment.
Ability to perform chemical and physical analyses accurately and consistently, following established procedures and Good Laboratory Practices.
Strong capability to organize work, manage multiple analyses, and meet testing schedules and deadlines.
Competence in collecting, preparing, and organizing samples for analysis with attention to detail and documentation.
Ability to interpret laboratory data, understand processing conditions, and communicate findings clearly to management and production teams.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Outlook for data entry, charting, reporting, and communication.
Bachelors degree in Biology, Chemistry, or a related science discipline.
Minimum of one year of laboratory work experience and/or experience in a quality-related field.
Awareness of food safety and allergen control practices, including familiarity with HACCP-related documentation and procedures.
Ability to work effectively as part of a team and to collaborate with quality, laboratory, and production personnel.

Experience working in a food processing, snack manufacturing, or plant-based product environment is beneficial.
Experience in applying Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and standard operating procedures (SOPs) in a production or laboratory setting.
Understanding of statistical process control (SPC) and experience creating and interpreting charts and graphs for process monitoring.
Ability to take initiative in monitoring inventory, identifying needs, and supporting continuous improvement in laboratory operations.

Modalities include LC-MS, GC-MS, MALDI-MS and MALDI Imaging MS. Major software applications include: Waters MassLynx, Thermo Scientific Chromeleon, Agilent MassHunter, Bruker flexcontrol and SCiLS Lab Pro and Shimadzu ImageReveal.

The incumbent will perform standardized laboratory and mass spectrometry research procedures, collect and organize experimental data, maintain research materials and MS equipment, and support ongoing research projects under close supervision.

Key Responsibilities

Research and Experimental Support: *Assist with laboratory experiments, method development, and research studies under the direction of faculty and senior research personnel. *Perform routine technical procedures according to established protocols, including procedures involving liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS), gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (MALDI-MS). *Prepare reagents, samples, cultures, and other research materials for laboratory experiments and analyses. *Collect, record, organize, and maintain experimental and observational data. *Maintain accurate and complete laboratory notebooks, research records, and associated databases. *Perform routine review and validation of research data, including small-molecule molecular formula validation and analyte identification. * Assist with literature searches and other research-related information gathering in support of laboratory projects. 60%

Laboratory Operations, Equipment Maintenance, and Safety: *Operate mass spectrometry and related laboratory equipment according to established procedures and protocols. *Perform routine instrument maintenance, including weekly maintenance activities and operation of quality control (QC) standards to support reliable instrument performance. *Clean and maintain laboratory instruments, equipment, and workspaces in accordance with established laboratory procedures. *Monitor laboratory supply and consumable inventories and coordinate routine ordering and restocking. *Follow laboratory safety procedures and applicable institutional requirements for the handling, storage, and disposal of research materials.*Properly collect and dispose of hazardous materials and laboratory waste in accordance with established institutional procedures. 20%

Research Documentation and Administrative Support: *Enter, verify, organize, and maintain research data and supporting documentation. *Prepare charts, spreadsheets, summaries, and other materials to support research activities and reporting. *Assist with preparation and maintenance of research documentation, records, and reports. *Provide routine coordination and scheduling support for laboratory and research activities as needed. 10%

Laboratory Training and Support: *Participate in laboratory meetings, technical training, and other activities necessary to maintain proficiency in laboratory procedures, instrumentation, research protocols, and safety requirements. *Complete required institutional and laboratory-specific safety and compliance training. *Assist with routine laboratory activities and operational needs that support the effective functioning of the research laboratory. * Perform other related duties as assigned consistent with the scope and level of the position. 10%

Job Description

The Department of Radiology is committed to excellence in patient care and inventing the future of Medical Diagnostics, Biomedical Imaging, and minimally invasive therapies. The people and programs comprising Stanford Radiology are world-renowned. Stanford Radiology continues to push the boundaries of innovation in physics and engineering to develop innovative methods for enhanced anatomic and functional imaging. Our diverse multidisciplinary teams of scientists, together with industry collaborators, are creating new methods for the early detection of cancer using molecular imaging, nanotechnology, and systems biology. They also continue to develop improved and more targeted methods for least invasive and compassionate cancer patient care. Ultimately, Stanford Radiology increasingly plays a very important role in the development of personalized medicine by moving advances from the laboratory to the clinic for improved patient centric care.

Stanford University is seeking a Life Science Research Professional 2 to perform more complex functions and activities involved in defined research projects, and independently conduct a portion of the research project(s).

Desired Qualifications

Equivalent working experience or Ph.D. in stem cell biology, immunology, or related field.
Post-doctoral experience is preferred in stem cell biology, cancer biology, immunology, or related field.
Extensive experience with molecular biology, mouse handling and procedures, flow-cytometry analysis and cell sorting, mammalian cell culture, RNA-sequencing, and microscopy.
Additional experience in computational biology is welcome.
Ability to independently design and troubleshoot experiments.
Excellent communication and organization skills.
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively.
Working knowledge of Microsoft Office, Adobe Illustrator, GraphPad Prism, R, and other related software.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS*:

Frequently stand, walk, twist, bend, stoop, squat, grasp lightly, use fine manipulation, grasp forcefully, perform desk-based computer tasks, use telephone, write by hand, lift, carry, push and pull objects weighing over 40 pounds.
Occasionally sit, kneel, crawl, reach and work above shoulders, sort and file paperwork or parts.
Rarely climb, scrub, sweep, mop, chop and mix or operate hand and foot controls.
Must have correctible vision to perform duties of the job.
Ability to bend, squat, kneel, stand, reach above shoulder level, and move on hard surfaces for up to eight hours.
Ability to lift heavy objects weighing up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work in a dusty, dirty, and odorous environment.
Position may require repetitive motion.
Consistent with its obligations under the law, the University will provide reasonable accommodation to any employee with a disability who requires accommodation to perform the essential functions of his or her job.

Working Conditions

May require working in close proximity to blood borne pathogens.
May require work in an environment where animals are used for teaching and research.
Position may at times require the employee to work with or be in areas where hazardous materials and/or infectious diseases are present.
Employee must perform tasks that require the use of personal protective equipment, such as safety glasses and shoes, protective clothing and gloves, and possibly a respirator.
May require extended or unusual work hours based on research requirements and business needs.

Work Standards

Interpersonal Skills: Demonstrates the ability to work well with Stanford colleagues and clients and with external organizations.
Promote Culture of Safety: Demonstrates commitment to personal responsibility and value for safety; communicates safety concerns; uses and promotes safe behaviors bases on training and lessons learned.
Subject to and expected to comply with all applicable University policies and procedures, including but not limited to the personnel policies and other policies found in the University’s Administrative Guide, http://adminguide.stanford.edu .

Responsibilities

Core Duties
:

Independently conduct a portion of the research project(s). Make recommendations on experimental design and/or research direction to principal investigator.
Independently conduct complex (lab and/or field) experiments to gather data for a portion of a major research project.
Interpret and analyze results, often where few guidelines exist, and make modifications to existing procedures and protocols.
Develop new research protocols where appropriate protocols are not described in the literature or where modification or adaptation of standard procedures and protocols is required.
Participate in multidisciplinary teams across different faculties or schools.
Perform ongoing literature review to remain current with new procedures and related research; apply to ongoing research and development of new protocols.
Contribute substantively to the preparation of papers for publication, especially in the results section, and to publication of findings. Present ongoing work to colleagues and/or academic conferences.
Oversee supply and equipment budget under supervision of principal investigator or business manager.
Work with health and safety department to ensure lab complies with regulations and all required trainings.
Supervise (either formally or informally) staff or students as needed, including oversight and direction on techniques, as well as consultation on project work. Serve as a technical resource for other research staff.
Oversee the daily activities of the laboratory including lab maintenance; maintain lab stock, manage chemical inventory and safety records, and provide general lab support as needed. May assist with purchasing laboratory equipment.

Minimum Education And Experience

Bachelor's degree in related scientific field and two years of relevant work experience; or Master’s degree in a related scientific field.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Comprehensive understanding of scientific principles.
General computer skills and ability to quickly learn and master computer programs, databases, and scientific applications.
Strong analytical skills and excellent judgment.
Ability to maintain detailed records of experiments and outcomes.
Ability to work under deadlines with general guidance is essential.
Excellent organizational skills and demonstrated ability to accurately complete detailed work.
